title: Introduce slotless autoscaler and burst-governor adapter
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a slotless autoscaling policy that enables fractional capacity allocation per tenant and a burst-governor adapter for microburst containment. Backwards compatible with existing reservation configs; recommended opt-in via feature flag. Includes telemetry and rollout knobs.
description:
Motivation:
Current autoscalers at Redwood operate on coarse-grained slots (min unit = slot). For workloads with many small sustained clients and intermittent microbursts, slots cause spiky prewarming, inefficient packing, and oscillatory scaling. This PR introduces a slotless autoscaler that can allocate fractional capacity units and a burst-governor adapter that limits short-duration microbursts while preserving sustained throughput guarantees. The goal is to reduce unnecessary warmup churn, smooth provisioning, and improve cost efficiency for multitenant Dedicated fleets.

What this change does (single-string summary):
- Implements a new scheduling policy: SlotlessAutoscaler (runtime/controller + API hooks).
- Adds BurstGovernorAdapter middleware that intercepts short-lived allocation requests and enforces a bounded burst budget per-tenant and per-pool.
- Introduces fractionalCapacity bookkeeping across the fleet ledger (stored as fixed-point values).
- Exposes new telemetry: fractional_allocations_total, burst_budget_used{tenant,pool}, slot_equivalents_allocated.
- Adds feature flags: feature.slotless_autoscaler (controller-side), feature.burst_governor (gateway-side).
- Migration: legacy slot reservations remain functional and are mapped to equivalent fractionalCapacity during rollouts.

Design highlights and algorithmic details:
- Fractional units: Internally we represent capacity in Q8 fixed-point (unit = 1/256 of a slot). The autoscaler computes target_capacity as a floating point value derived from d(throughput)/p(per-slot-throughput), then converts to fixed point. This lets the allocator pack tenants without strictly rounding up to whole slots, reducing overprovisioning.
- Smoothing windows: A multi-timescale EWMA is used (fast=5s, med=60s, slow=10m) to separate microbursts from sustained load. The autoscaler is conservative towards the slow EWMA for scale-down decisions and uses fast+med for scale-up.
- BurstGovernorAdapter: Each tenant has a soft burst budget that refills linearly (1 token per 100ms of baseline slot-equivalent). Microbursts draw from this budget; if budget exhausted the adapter will: (1) apply short delay jittering (configurable up to 200ms), (2) optionally spill requests to a best-effort pool, or (3) gracefully throttle at a configured p99 latency degradation target. The adapter is pluggable per-pool via pool config.
- Safety and fallbacks: When fractional bookkeeping or the slotless policy is disabled (feature toggle), we map fractional allocations up to the nearest slot and trigger a warmup plan identical to legacy behavior. For tenants with hard reservation contracts the allocator respects reserved floor and only uses fractional elasticity for the burstable portion.

APIs and config (example knobs):
- cluster.autoscaler.policy: "slotless" | "sloted"
- cluster.autoscaler.slotless.max_fraction_per_tenant: "8.0"  # max slots a tenant can accrue as fractional units
- pool.burst_governor.burst_budget_ms_per_minute: "8000"  # how many ms of burst-equivalent allowed per minute
- pool.burst_governor.jitter_ms: "200"
- feature flags: rollout via operations toggle: opsctl feature enable slotless_autoscaler --env=staging

Files changed (high-level):
- runtime/autoscaler/slotless_controller.go  (new) -- core slotless autoscaler loop, allocation math
- runtime/autoscaler/quant_fsm.go (new) -- fixed-point helpers and unit tests
- gateway/adapters/burst_governor.go (new) -- middleware implementation and config parsing
- controllers/migration/slotless_mapping.go (new) -- mapping legacy reservations to fractional ledger entries
- observability/metrics/slotless_metrics.yaml (new) -- dashboard and alert hints
- docs/operators/slotless-autoscaler.md (new) -- operator guide and rollout steps
- tests/integration/slotless_endtoend_test.go (new) -- flow tests with simulated tenants
- charts/values.yaml (updated) -- feature flag defaults and defaults for pool adapters

Commits (summary):
- Add fixed-point fractional capacity helpers and unit tests
- Implement slotless controller allocation loop and tests for EWMA smoothing
- Implement burst governor adapter, integrate with gateway, add config parsing
- Add migration mapping of legacy slots to fractional ledger on startup
- Add metrics and dashboards; update charts and docs
- Fix race in ledger update; add lock around fractional balance write

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests cover arithmetic edge-cases (saturation/overflow), refill logic for burst budgets, and EWMA behavior.
- Integration tests simulate 120 tenants with mixed traffic patterns (steady + microbursts) and assert: tail latency targets, reduced total provisioned slot-equivalents (>= 12% improvement in the sim), and no regression on hard reservation tenants.
- Load tests (local perf-lab) indicate a 9–15% reduction in GPU warmups under typical PLG traffic traces.
- CI history: initial pipeline (run 2026-02-11) failed lint due to docstring style; fixed on commit #4. One flaky integration test (TestBurstBudgetRefill) failed intermittently in CI on 2026-02-14; root cause was a time.Now() dependency—replaced with clock interface and stabilized. Final CI run shows all checks passing.

Rollout plan and canary:
- Feature-gate approach: enable slotless_autoscaler in staging 25% of capacity for 72h, monitor slot_equivalents_allocated and burst_budget_used heatmaps.
- Canary metrics to watch: provisioning churn (warmups/min), fleet fractional_utilization_ratio (expected +), tenant p99 latency, and ingest rate of ledger-change errors.
- If p99 latency for any tenant degrades > 5% against baseline for 30m, rollback the feature flag and escalate to SRE.

Review conversation (selected):
- Arjun Patel (reviewer): "Can we avoid per-request locks on the fractional ledger? The earlier implementation had a global lock which hurt concurrency."
- Author reply (Maya): "Good call — added per-tenant sharded locks and an optimistic update path. See quant_fsm.go: UpdateFractionalWithCAS. Added unit test for concurrent updates."
- Sofia Martinez: "Please add an operator-facing dashboard widget that shows burst budget exhaustion by tenant — Ops asked for an easy triage surface."
- Author reply: "Added slotless_metrics.yaml and a Grafana panel sample. Also added an alert: alert_burst_budget_exhausted_count > 5 for 5m."
- Liam O'Connor: "The refill rate constants feel aggressive for very spiky traffic; consider exposing per-tenant multiplier."
- Author reply: "Exposed pool.burst_governor.burst_multiplier and documented recommended defaults. Also added a note to docs/operators/slotless-autoscaler.md."

Backward compatibility notes:
- No change required for clients calling Redwood API. All changes are internal to fleet orchestration and gateway middleware.
- Reservation semantics: tenants with hard committed slots will see the same guaranteed baseline; any elastic upswing will use fractional units.

Operational telemetry added:
- fractional_allocations_total{tenant,pool} (counter)
- fractional_allocated_gauge{pool} (gauge)
- burst_budget_used_total{tenant,pool} (counter)
- burst_budget_exhausted_count{tenant,pool} (counter)
- slot_equivalents_allocated (derived metric for dashboards)

Known limitations and follow-ups (tracked in ENG-8470):
- Current implementation maps fractional units to single-cluster pool; cross-cluster fractional rebalancing will be a follow-up (RFC planned).
- The chosen fixed-point Q8 may need review if we onboard extremely high slot counts; a perf patch to move to Q12 is logged.
- More sophisticated proportional fairness among tenants under extreme contention is future work (see follow-up ENG-8555).

Why this is unique / expected impact:
- By removing whole-slot granularity we reduce forced warmups and can more tightly pack tenants, resulting in measurable cost and latency improvements for PLG-style tenant mixes. The burst-governor protects the fleet from microburst storms while maintaining SLA for reserved throughput.

Contact/owners: Maya Chen (author), Arjun Patel (autoscaler), SRE on-call (rotation).

If merged: ops will flip the feature in staging and run the 72h canary. Documentation is included with operator runbooks and rollback steps.
